query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of controlled chemical ordering in the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy through substitutional solutes can enhance its mechanical properties without sacrificing caloric response.
generation.intervention: Addition of substitutional solutes (e.g., Al, Ti) to introduce chemical ordering tendency
generation.conditions: Applied-field, pressure-field operation, and various temperature and loading regimes
generation.structural_mediator: Chemical ordering, including short-range order (SRO) and long-range order (LRO)
generation.mechanism: Enhancement of mechanical properties due to introduction of chemical ordering, which correlates with systematic increase in mechanical properties
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical properties (e.g., yield strength, ductility) without sacrificing caloric response
generation.boundary: Applied-field, pressure-field operation, and various temperature and loading regimes
generation.uncertainty: Optimal composition and processing conditions for introducing chemical ordering, and potential impact on caloric response

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment with varying substitutional solute contents and processing conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If introduction of chemical ordering does not enhance mechanical properties without sacrificing caloric response, the hypothesis is falsified.

Mechanical properties of single-phase high-entropy alloys (HEAs) can be unusually enhanced than many conventional single-phase engineering alloys (). Recent computational and experimental studies indicate that the atomic distribution in such solid solution HEAs may not be completely random as originally believed, but exhibit localized pockets of nonrandom distributions, also called “clustered ordering” (). While strengthening due to such local chemical clusters has been reported in Al (), Ni (), Fe () base alloys, and more recently, in complex bulk metallic glasses () and HEAs (, ), the ability to systematically engineer its nature and extent has so far eluded us.
While the quinary CoCrFeNiMn, arguably the most extensively studied HEA, has been established as a single-phase alloy (), local chemical ordering was recently experimentally shown, and computationally validated, in its “subset” ternary CoCrNi alloy (, ) Similarly, direct experimental evidence of nonrandom atomic distributions has been presented in CoCrFeNiPd () and CoNiV () HEAs. We hypothesized that controlled additions of Al and Ti to the base CoFeNi random solid solution can introduce and progressively increase the extent of local chemical ordering, thereby modifying its mechanical response. Our hypothesis was tested via detailed investigations in four different alloys—CoFeNi (33Co-33Fe-33Ni at.%), Al0.25CoFeNi (7.6Al-30.8Co-30.8Fe-30.8Ni at.%), Al0.3CoFeNi (9.1Al-30.3Co-30.3Fe-30.3Ni at.%), and Al0.3Ti0.2CoFeNi (8.5Al-5.7Ti-28.6Co-28.6Fe-28.6Ni at.%). The compositions were chosen such that the transition from SRO tendency to fully developed long-range order (LRO) can be examined. These alloys were first homogenized and solution treated at 1,200 °C for 5 min within the single FCC phase field and then water-quenched to room temperature. The temperature was chosen based on the pseudobinary isopleths obtained from solution thermodynamic modeling (SI Appendix, Fig. S1). To overcome the prohibitive computational costs of very large supercells in DFT calculations, we generated both 108-atom and 216-atom special quasirandom structures (SQSs) (, ) to model the FCC Al0.27CoFeNi alloy with SRO. As shown in SI Appendix, Table S3, the pair correlation functions of our SQSs agree well with those of the short-range ordered alloy predicted by our MC simulations. For comparison, SQSs for the completely random Al0.27CoFeNi alloy were also created to closely reproduce the pair correlation functions of the random alloy (SI Appendix, Table S4). The pair distribution functions of the random and SRO Al0.27CoFeNi alloy are shown in Fig. 2 E and F, respectively. Our DFT calculations with 216 (108)-atom SQSs indicate that, at 1200°C, SRO can reduce the total energy of the Al0.27CoFeNi alloy by 0.118 (0.200) eV per Al atom.
